summary:
Galicia is an autonomous community of Spain, and the national framework set by Ley 4/2023 of 28 February 2023, the organic law on real and effective equality for trans persons and the guarantee of LGBTI rights, governs legal gender recognition and protection against LGBTIphobic discrimination in the region as it does in the rest of the country.

The statute assigns implementation of its education-facing and administrative provisions to the autonomous communities. The Xunta de Galicia is one of the regional governments charged with carrying them out, and public authorities in Galicia act within their own competences when they do so. How the region's schools, administrative services and public bodies apply those provisions determines what trans residents and visitors meet in practice, and the sources reviewed do not describe Galicia's implementation record.

Galicia's courts have produced the first application of the discrimination aggravating circumstance for transfobia recorded in the country. In July 2026 the Tribunal de Instancia in Vigo fined the author of WhatsApp messages that threatened a trans woman EUR 300. The conviction was a misdemeanour, and it is the only documented regional enforcement of that aggravating circumstance in the sources reviewed.

Nothing in the sources reviewed documents region-specific legislation or practice in Galicia that restricts trans visitors. Recognition, document markers, facility access and healthcare access are governed by the national law, and no Galicia-level measure narrowing them appears.
tangentialFactors:
Comparison between Galicia and other parts of Spain is limited by what the sources document. Protection levels differ between the country's autonomous communities, and that variation belongs to the national picture rather than to Galicia, which the sources do not describe as having narrowed or expanded the national rules. For Galicia the sources record no trans-rights statute of its own and no divergence from the national recognition and facility-access rules.

The one documented legal development in the region is judicial rather than legislative: the Vigo first-instance ruling applying the discrimination aggravating circumstance, the first of its kind in the country, with no successor rulings in Galicia recorded in the inventory.
localsOnly:
Implementation of the education-facing and administrative provisions of the national law falls to the autonomous communities. In Galicia the Xunta de Galicia holds that role and acts within its own competences, so access to the measures the law creates in schools, administrative procedure and regional public services depends on regional implementation rather than on any separate Galicia statute.

A resident reporting a transphobic threat in Galicia can expect it to be prosecutable with the discrimination aggravating circumstance attached, as the July 2026 Vigo ruling shows. The sources reviewed describe no complaint mechanism specific to Galicia beyond the national one.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Galicia-specific non-discrimination or trans-rights statute appears in the sources reviewed; the regional layer is the implementation of Ley 4/2023 by the Xunta de Galicia within its own competences.

Whether the Xunta de Galicia has adopted implementing plans, protocols or funding for the law's education-facing and administrative provisions is not sourced. Regional statistics on anti-LGBTI or anti-trans incidents in Galicia, and any regional guidance for courts, police or healthcare on the discrimination aggravating circumstance, were not found in the inventory.

Recognition procedure, document markers and facility access in Galicia are set by the national law and not by the autonomous community.
